- criteria_path: /home/vscode/rebaseline/basis/fitness/adr.fitness.md

Read the criteria set at criteria_path, the architecture principle set at principles, and the artifact at artifact — nothing else. Judge the artifact against every criterion and against the principle set: does the decision conform to each principle, or does the record name the principle it cannot satisfy with its escalation? judge_stamp: <model id> / screen prompt v6
verdict: clean | findings
findings:
- criterion: <scenario name or number, a principle's name, or "uncovered">
  section: <section of the artifact>
  quoted: "<the text>"
  change: <what would repair it>
  decided: confident | wobbly
top_three: <the three most important changes, or "none">

Be literal to the criteria and the principles. Do not invent criteria. Do not read any other file.

14	
15	# Architecture principles
16	
17	## What this set governs
18	
19	This is the architecture-scope principle set: the standing rules for how
20	the product is designed — its regions, their boundaries, and the entities
21	that build and evolve them. It is a peer of the working-scope set,
22	[Founding principles](principles.md), which governs how every activity is
23	performed; this set governs what the designed system must look like.
24	Backticked slugs cite principles; a slug not defined in this document is
25	defined in the working set. The terms Bounded Context, shop, activity,
26	contract, relationship kind, and intent are defined in the
27	[glossary](glossary.md). Two distinctions those terms carry are used
28	throughout. A shop is either the lead shop — the system-level
29	coordinator, owning the product-level artifacts and no Bounded
30	Context — or a BC-shop, owning exactly one. A contract is offered
31	either as a product contract, on a Bounded Context, or as an
32	operational contract, on a shop.
33	
34	Where a principle here applies a working-scope principle at the
35	architecture level, this document declares the lineage in its
36	frontmatter — `derives-from` maps the principle in this set to the
37	working-scope principle it applies — instead of restating the rule as a
38	second authority.
39	
40	## What a good principle looks like
41	
42	This section restates the shared definition from the
43	[principle-set typedef](artifacts/principle-set.md) so this document can
44	be read alone; the restatement is a rendering, not a second authority.
45	
46	A principle is a standing rule, in four parts: a name, a statement, a
47	rationale, and implications.
48	
49	- The **statement** is the rule. It carries the only normative keywords
50	  (MUST, SHOULD, MAY — interpreted per BCP 14 when, and only when, they
51	  appear in capitals) and is testable: shown a piece of work, you can
52	  answer yes or no. A statement carrying more than one obligation
53	  presents one obligation per bullet.
54	- The **rationale** says why the rule earns its place: the failure it
55	  prevents, shown as a generic example; well-known external references
56	  may support it, the product's own history never appears. Rationales
57	  stay prose.
58	- The **implications** are the price tag: one implication per bullet,
59	  the concrete change each named actor absorbs to honor the rule. They
60	  add no obligations — every implication must be derivable from the
61	  statement, or it is a misfiled rule.
62	
63	A principle is good when its statement is testable (TOGAF, The Open
64	Group Architecture Framework: understandable, complete, consistent), it
65	rejects work we would otherwise do (Jared Spool, "Creating Great Design
66	Principles"), it directs without prescribing method (Richard Rumelt,
67	*Good Strategy Bad Strategy*), it is not a claim every shop would make
68	(Patrick Lencioni, "Make Your Values Mean Something", Harvard Business
69	Review, 2002), and it implies at least one practice and one check. The fitness screen at the
70	end of this document applies these tests to the principles above it.
71	
72	---
73	
74	## Every first-class entity has a knowable shape (`knowable-shape`)
75	
76	**Statement.**
77	
78	- The product MUST have exactly two kinds of first-class entity: the
79	  Bounded Context and the shop.
80	- Each Bounded Context MUST be contained and produced by exactly one
81	  BC-shop; the lead shop MUST NOT contain one.
82	- Every first-class entity MUST carry a description, maintained as an
83	  artifact, from which an outside reader can name what the entity is
84	  for, what it accepts and produces, what it guarantees, and the
85	  contracts it offers.
86	- The description MUST suffice without reading the entity's internal
87	  code or configuration and without asking its maintainers.
88	
89	**Rationale.** When an entity's shape lives only in its internals, every
90	consumer, coordinator, and reviewer pays to rediscover it, and each
91	rediscovery reaches a different answer: nobody can say what a service
92	guarantees without opening its source, the answer holds only until the
93	next commit, and no description can be trusted without re-inspecting
94	the thing it describes. Parnas made the design case in 1972: a module
95	is known by what its interface states, not by what its implementation
96	happens to do. Without `knowable-shape`,
97	`contracts-between-contexts` is speculative — no one can write a
98	contract for an entity whose shape no one can state.
99	
100	**Implications.**
101	
102	- Whoever creates a Bounded Context or a shop writes its description at
103	  creation; an entity without a description is not yet created,
104	  whatever code exists.
105	- Maintainers keep the description authoritative: when an outside
106	  reader must open internals to answer a question the description
107	  claims to cover, the description is the defect and its maintainer
108	  repairs it.
109	- Architects reason from descriptions; opening an entity's internals is
110	  audit work — checking that a description is true — not the normal way
111	  to learn what the entity is.
112	
113	## Contracts are the only channel between Bounded Contexts (`contracts-between-contexts`)
114	
115	**Statement.**
116	
117	- Anything one Bounded Context expects of another MUST pass through a
118	  named, versioned contract stating the schemas exchanged, the meaning
119	  of each operation, the error behavior, and the relationship kind.
120	- A Bounded Context MUST NOT rely on anything its counterpart's
121	  contract does not state.
122	- Bounded Contexts MUST NOT share state or coordinate outside their
123	  contracts.
124	
125	**Rationale.** Unstated expectations cannot be reviewed, versioned, or
126	deliberately kept — they are discovered when they break. Hyrum's law
127	(Winters, Manshreck, and Wright, *Software Engineering at Google*)
128	records the observed endpoint: with enough consumers, every observable
129	behavior of a system will be depended on by somebody, whatever the
130	contract says — the only defense is making the contract the sole thing a
131	consumer is entitled to. Evans (*Domain-Driven Design*, 2003) draws
132	context boundaries for the same reason: models stay coherent only when
133	what crosses between them is explicit. Without this rule,
134	`local-comprehension` collapses — a consumer must read a counterpart's
135	internals to learn what is safe to use.
136	
137	**Implications.**
138	
139	- Contract authors put every promise in the contract document —
140	  schemas, semantics, errors, relationship kind; a promise made
141	  anywhere else is not owed.
142	- Reviewers of a consuming context treat reliance on unstated behavior
143	  as that context's defect, and treat the underlying need as a
144	  contract-change request, not a license to work around the contract.
145	- Integrators who need a channel the contract lacks amend the contract
146	  first or do not integrate.
147	
148	## Discipline attaches to activities, not actors (`actor-neutral-discipline`)
149	
150	**Statement.**
151	
152	- Rules, authority, and required records MUST attach to the activity
153	  and the role performing it, never to the kind of actor filling the
154	  role.
155	- An activity MUST NOT record less, skip checks, or gain authority
156	  because a particular kind of actor — human, agent, or service —
157	  performs it.
158	
159	**Rationale.** Rules forked by actor kind create bypasses: whichever
160	fork is weakest becomes the route around the discipline, and social
161	routes — "just ask the team next door" — are exactly the moves agents
162	scale beyond anyone's review. Role-based access control (Ferraiolo and
163	Kuhn, 1992; the NIST RBAC model) grounds the mechanism: grant to roles,
164	and the actor mix can change without regranting authority. The working
165	set's `no-orphan-activities` already places every activity in a process;
166	this rule keeps those processes actor-neutral, which is what keeps
167	`contracts-between-contexts` binding on whoever shows up — an actor that
168	could renegotiate the rules by kind could talk its way around a
169	contract.
170	
171	**Implications.**
172	
173	- Process authors demand the same inputs, checks, and records from a
174	  step whoever performs it; "it was just an automation" excuses no
175	  missing record.
176	- Reviewers strike rule text that splits one activity by actor kind —
177	  "humans may, agents must" — the rule attaches to the activity or it
178	  goes.
179	- Whoever grants authority grants it to a role within a process; a
180	  standing grant to an individual actor is a defect whoever holds it.
181	
182	## Comprehension is local at every level (`local-comprehension`)
183	
184	**Statement.**
185	
186	- A participant MUST NOT need to read beyond the level they are
187	  working at.
188	- The design MUST designate, for each level, the description artifacts
189	  sufficient for that level's work. The levels, and their designated
190	  artifacts, are (a closed set):
191	  - working inside a shop — that shop's own records and code;
192	  - consuming a Bounded Context — that context's contracts;
193	  - working across Bounded Contexts — the contracts and the
194	    system-level map of the contexts and their relationships;
195	  - coordinating the system — the product-level descriptions the lead
196	    shop owns.
197	- Work at a level MUST be performable from its designated artifacts
198	  alone.
199	- A task that can be done only by reading below its level MUST be
200	  treated as a design defect — a missing or incomplete description or
201	  contract — not as the reader's burden.
202	
203	**Rationale.** The cost of working on one part of the product has to
204	stay proportional to that part, or growth taxes every participant; for
205	agents the tax is literal — context loaded is context paid for. The
206	familiar endpoint of the failure: a corpus with no designated reading
207	levels grows until a one-line change is one nobody dares make without
208	reading the whole system first, and every newcomer must read far beyond
209	the task at hand before starting it. This rule applies the
210	working set's `least-context` to the designed system — the lineage is
211	declared in this document's frontmatter: `least-context` caps what an
212	activity loads, and a design obeying this rule is what makes that cap
213	reachable, because the artifacts an activity needs exist at its own
214	level.
215	
216	**Implications.**
217	
218	- Designers ship each level's designated artifacts as part of the
219	  design; a level whose work demands undesignated reading is unfinished
220	  design.
221	- Whoever hits a task that requires reading below its level files the
222	  defect against the design and does not normalize the deep read into
223	  practice.
224	- Reviewers of a design check the reading bound: the artifacts a task
225	  needs stay proportional to the task's level, not to the product's
226	  size.
227	
228	## Design is authoritative, conformance runs both ways (`bidirectional-conformance`)
229	
230	**Statement.**
231	
232	- The design — descriptions, contracts, recorded decisions — MUST be
233	  the authoritative statement of what the product is and does, and code
234	  MUST conform to it.
235	- Conformance MUST be checked in both directions: forward — every
236	  design element MUST have code implementing it (did we build what we
237	  said?) — and reverse — every code element MUST be called for by the
238	  design (did we build only what we said?).
239	- A design change MUST itself be a recorded activity.
240	- Retirement and refactoring MUST be gated on both conformance checks.
241	
242	**Rationale.** When code is the authority, descriptions decay into
243	folklore and `knowable-shape` drifts false — the description stops
244	matching the entity it claims to describe. Forward checking alone
245	misses half the failure: features removed on paper live on as unowned
246	code, and undecided behavior accumulates until the design describes a
247	product that no longer exists. Murphy, Notkin, and Sullivan's reflexion
248	models (1995) demonstrated the two-directional comparison this
249	statement requires — computing both what the design promises that the
250	code lacks, and what the code contains that the design never called
251	for. The working set holds the two flanking rules at working scope:
252	`single-source-of-truth` gives every fact one authoritative home, and
253	`delivery-verified` demands the forward direction be demonstrated in
254	the running system; this rule adds the reverse direction and gates
255	retirement and refactoring on the pair.
256	
257	**Implications.**
258	
259	- Whoever changes behavior records the design change — before the code
260	  change or in the same recorded activity; silent drift is reverted,
261	  never adopted after the fact.
262	- Whoever retires a feature removes it from the design first; the
263	  reverse check then names the code that may be deleted, and nothing
264	  else is.
265	- Refactorers demonstrate both checks unchanged — no behavior lost
266	  forward, none gained in reverse.
267	- Reviewers reject code no design element calls for, however good it
268	  is.
269	
270	## Intent enters through contracts and keeps its provenance (`intent-provenance`)
271	
272	**Statement.**
273	
274	- Intent — a desired outcome expressed by an originator at the
275	  product's edge — MUST enter the product through a contract: a product
276	  contract on a Bounded Context or an operational contract on a shop.
277	- The shop that receives intent MAY translate it, and MAY delegate it
278	  to other shops, only ever through those shops' contracts.
279	- Every receipt, translation, and delegation MUST be recorded, so that
280	  any activity can be traced back to the originating expression without
281	  ambiguity.
282	
283	**Rationale.** Intent that loses its origin cannot be re-decided: when
284	priorities shift, no one can tell which work still serves a live desire
285	and which serves a decision nobody remembers making — "why did we build
286	this?" becomes answerable only by whoever happened to be present.
287	IEEE 29148 (requirements engineering) standardizes exactly the chain
288	this statement demands: each requirement traceable to its source and to
289	what implements it. Routing intent through contracts keeps
290	`contracts-between-contexts` whole at the product's edge — a backlog
291	living outside the product's contracts is an out-of-band channel like
292	any other, aimed at the builders instead of the contexts. And the trace
293	is what gives `bidirectional-conformance` its meaning: conformance can
294	verify that code matches design, but only provenance can verify that
295	either matches what anyone asked for.
296	
297	**Implications.**
298	
299	- Whoever accepts intent records it at the contract where it entered
300	  before working on it.
301	- Whoever translates or delegates intent records each translation
302	  against the original, at every step.
303	- Reviewers may demand the originator chain for any activity; a trace
304	  that dead-ends is a recording defect to repair, not a question to
305	  drop.
306	
307	---
308	
309	## Fitness screen (the intro's tests; sources: TOGAF, Spool, Rumelt, Lencioni)
310	
311	| Screen | knowable-shape | contracts-between-contexts | actor-neutral-discipline | local-comprehension | bidirectional-conformance | intent-provenance |

# Architecture principles

## What this set governs

This is the architecture-scope principle set: the standing rules for how
the product is designed — its regions, their boundaries, and the entities
that build and evolve them. It is a peer of the working-scope set,
[Founding principles](principles.md), which governs how every activity is
performed; this set governs what the designed system must look like.
Backticked slugs cite principles; a slug not defined in this document is
defined in the working set. The terms Bounded Context, shop, activity,
contract, relationship kind, and intent are defined in the
[glossary](glossary.md). Two distinctions those terms carry are used
throughout. A shop is either the lead shop — the system-level
coordinator, owning the product-level artifacts and no Bounded
Context — or a BC-shop, owning exactly one. A contract is offered
either as a product contract, on a Bounded Context, or as an
operational contract, on a shop.

Where a principle here applies a working-scope principle at the
architecture level, this document declares the lineage in its
frontmatter — `derives-from` maps the principle in this set to the
working-scope principle it applies — instead of restating the rule as a
second authority.

## What a good principle looks like

This section restates the shared definition from the
[principle-set typedef](artifacts/principle-set.md) so this document can
be read alone; the restatement is a rendering, not a second authority.

A principle is a standing rule, in four parts: a name, a statement, a
rationale, and implications.

- The **statement** is the rule. It carries the only normative keywords
  (MUST, SHOULD, MAY — interpreted per BCP 14 when, and only when, they
  appear in capitals) and is testable: shown a piece of work, you can
  answer yes or no. A statement carrying more than one obligation
  presents one obligation per bullet.
- The **rationale** says why the rule earns its place: the failure it
  prevents, shown as a generic example; well-known external references
  may support it, the product's own history never appears. Rationales
  stay prose.
- The **implications** are the price tag: one implication per bullet,
  the concrete change each named actor absorbs to honor the rule. They
  add no obligations — every implication must be derivable from the
  statement, or it is a misfiled rule.

A principle is good when its statement is testable (TOGAF, The Open
Group Architecture Framework: understandable, complete, consistent), it
rejects work we would otherwise do (Jared Spool, "Creating Great Design
Principles"), it directs without prescribing method (Richard Rumelt,
*Good Strategy Bad Strategy*), it is not a claim every shop would make
(Patrick Lencioni, "Make Your Values Mean Something", Harvard Business
Review, 2002), and it implies at least one practice and one check. The fitness screen at the
end of this document applies these tests to the principles above it.

---

## Every first-class entity has a knowable shape (`knowable-shape`)

**Statement.**

- The product MUST have exactly two kinds of first-class entity: the
  Bounded Context and the shop.
- Each Bounded Context MUST be contained and produced by exactly one
  BC-shop; the lead shop MUST NOT contain one.
- Every first-class entity MUST carry a description, maintained as an
  artifact, from which an outside reader can name what the entity is
  for, what it accepts and produces, what it guarantees, and the
  contracts it offers.
- The description MUST suffice without reading the entity's internal
  code or configuration and without asking its maintainers.

**Rationale.** When an entity's shape lives only in its internals, every
consumer, coordinator, and reviewer pays to rediscover it, and each
rediscovery reaches a different answer: nobody can say what a service
guarantees without opening its source, the answer holds only until the
next commit, and no description can be trusted without re-inspecting
the thing it describes. Parnas made the design case in 1972: a module
is known by what its interface states, not by what its implementation
happens to do. Without `knowable-shape`,
`contracts-between-contexts` is speculative — no one can write a
contract for an entity whose shape no one can state.

**Implications.**

- Whoever creates a Bounded Context or a shop writes its description at
  creation; an entity without a description is not yet created,
  whatever code exists.
- Maintainers keep the description authoritative: when an outside
  reader must open internals to answer a question the description
  claims to cover, the description is the defect and its maintainer
  repairs it.
- Architects reason from descriptions; opening an entity's internals is
  audit work — checking that a description is true — not the normal way
  to learn what the entity is.

## Contracts are the only channel between Bounded Contexts (`contracts-between-contexts`)

**Statement.**

- Anything one Bounded Context expects of another MUST pass through a
  named, versioned contract stating the schemas exchanged, the meaning
  of each operation, the error behavior, and the relationship kind.
- A Bounded Context MUST NOT rely on anything its counterpart's
  contract does not state.
- Bounded Contexts MUST NOT share state or coordinate outside their
  contracts.

**Rationale.** Unstated expectations cannot be reviewed, versioned, or
deliberately kept — they are discovered when they break. Hyrum's law
(Winters, Manshreck, and Wright, *Software Engineering at Google*)
records the observed endpoint: with enough consumers, every observable
behavior of a system will be depended on by somebody, whatever the
contract says — the only defense is making the contract the sole thing a
consumer is entitled to. Evans (*Domain-Driven Design*, 2003) draws
context boundaries for the same reason: models stay coherent only when
what crosses between them is explicit. Without this rule,
`local-comprehension` collapses — a consumer must read a counterpart's
internals to learn what is safe to use.

**Implications.**

- Contract authors put every promise in the contract document —
  schemas, semantics, errors, relationship kind; a promise made
  anywhere else is not owed.
- Reviewers of a consuming context treat reliance on unstated behavior
  as that context's defect, and treat the underlying need as a
  contract-change request, not a license to work around the contract.
- Integrators who need a channel the contract lacks amend the contract
  first or do not integrate.

## Discipline attaches to activities, not actors (`actor-neutral-discipline`)

**Statement.**

- Rules, authority, and required records MUST attach to the activity
  and the role performing it, never to the kind of actor filling the
  role.
- An activity MUST NOT record less, skip checks, or gain authority
  because a particular kind of actor — human, agent, or service —
  performs it.

**Rationale.** Rules forked by actor kind create bypasses: whichever
fork is weakest becomes the route around the discipline, and social
routes — "just ask the team next door" — are exactly the moves agents
scale beyond anyone's review. Role-based access control (Ferraiolo and
Kuhn, 1992; the NIST RBAC model) grounds the mechanism: grant to roles,
and the actor mix can change without regranting authority. The working
set's `no-orphan-activities` already places every activity in a process;
this rule keeps those processes actor-neutral, which is what keeps
`contracts-between-contexts` binding on whoever shows up — an actor that
could renegotiate the rules by kind could talk its way around a
contract.

**Implications.**

- Process authors demand the same inputs, checks, and records from a
  step whoever performs it; "it was just an automation" excuses no
  missing record.
- Reviewers strike rule text that splits one activity by actor kind —
  "humans may, agents must" — the rule attaches to the activity or it
  goes.
- Whoever grants authority grants it to a role within a process; a
  standing grant to an individual actor is a defect whoever holds it.

## Comprehension is local at every level (`local-comprehension`)

**Statement.**

- A participant MUST NOT need to read beyond the level they are
  working at.
- The design MUST designate, for each level, the description artifacts
  sufficient for that level's work. The levels, and their designated
  artifacts, are (a closed set):
  - working inside a shop — that shop's own records and code;
  - consuming a Bounded Context — that context's contracts;
  - working across Bounded Contexts — the contracts and the
    system-level map of the contexts and their relationships;
  - coordinating the system — the product-level descriptions the lead
    shop owns.
- Work at a level MUST be performable from its designated artifacts
  alone.
- A task that can be done only by reading below its level MUST be
  treated as a design defect — a missing or incomplete description or
  contract — not as the reader's burden.

**Rationale.** The cost of working on one part of the product has to
stay proportional to that part, or growth taxes every participant; for
agents the tax is literal — context loaded is context paid for. The
familiar endpoint of the failure: a corpus with no designated reading
levels grows until a one-line change is one nobody dares make without
reading the whole system first, and every newcomer must read far beyond
the task at hand before starting it. This rule applies the
working set's `least-context` to the designed system — the lineage is
declared in this document's frontmatter: `least-context` caps what an
activity loads, and a design obeying this rule is what makes that cap
reachable, because the artifacts an activity needs exist at its own
level.

**Implications.**

- Designers ship each level's designated artifacts as part of the
  design; a level whose work demands undesignated reading is unfinished
  design.
- Whoever hits a task that requires reading below its level files the
  defect against the design and does not normalize the deep read into
  practice.
- Reviewers of a design check the reading bound: the artifacts a task
  needs stay proportional to the task's level, not to the product's
  size.

## Design is authoritative, conformance runs both ways (`bidirectional-conformance`)

**Statement.**

- The design — descriptions, contracts, recorded decisions — MUST be
  the authoritative statement of what the product is and does, and code
  MUST conform to it.
- Conformance MUST be checked in both directions: forward — every
  design element MUST have code implementing it (did we build what we
  said?) — and reverse — every code element MUST be called for by the
  design (did we build only what we said?).
- A design change MUST itself be a recorded activity.
- Retirement and refactoring MUST be gated on both conformance checks.

**Rationale.** When code is the authority, descriptions decay into
folklore and `knowable-shape` drifts false — the description stops
matching the entity it claims to describe. Forward checking alone
misses half the failure: features removed on paper live on as unowned
code, and undecided behavior accumulates until the design describes a
product that no longer exists. Murphy, Notkin, and Sullivan's reflexion
models (1995) demonstrated the two-directional comparison this
statement requires — computing both what the design promises that the
code lacks, and what the code contains that the design never called
for. The working set holds the two flanking rules at working scope:
`single-source-of-truth` gives every fact one authoritative home, and
`delivery-verified` demands the forward direction be demonstrated in
the running system; this rule adds the reverse direction and gates
retirement and refactoring on the pair.

**Implications.**

- Whoever changes behavior records the design change — before the code
  change or in the same recorded activity; silent drift is reverted,
  never adopted after the fact.
- Whoever retires a feature removes it from the design first; the
  reverse check then names the code that may be deleted, and nothing
  else is.
- Refactorers demonstrate both checks unchanged — no behavior lost
  forward, none gained in reverse.
- Reviewers reject code no design element calls for, however good it
  is.

## Intent enters through contracts and keeps its provenance (`intent-provenance`)

**Statement.**

- Intent — a desired outcome expressed by an originator at the
  product's edge — MUST enter the product through a contract: a product
  contract on a Bounded Context or an operational contract on a shop.
- The shop that receives intent MAY translate it, and MAY delegate it
  to other shops, only ever through those shops' contracts.
- Every receipt, translation, and delegation MUST be recorded, so that
  any activity can be traced back to the originating expression without
  ambiguity.

**Rationale.** Intent that loses its origin cannot be re-decided: when
priorities shift, no one can tell which work still serves a live desire
and which serves a decision nobody remembers making — "why did we build
this?" becomes answerable only by whoever happened to be present.
IEEE 29148 (requirements engineering) standardizes exactly the chain
this statement demands: each requirement traceable to its source and to
what implements it. Routing intent through contracts keeps
`contracts-between-contexts` whole at the product's edge — a backlog
living outside the product's contracts is an out-of-band channel like
any other, aimed at the builders instead of the contexts. And the trace
is what gives `bidirectional-conformance` its meaning: conformance can
verify that code matches design, but only provenance can verify that
either matches what anyone asked for.

**Implications.**

- Whoever accepts intent records it at the contract where it entered
  before working on it.
- Whoever translates or delegates intent records each translation
  against the original, at every step.
- Reviewers may demand the originator chain for any activity; a trace
  that dead-ends is a recording defect to repair, not a question to
  drop.

---

## Fitness screen (the intro's tests; sources: TOGAF, Spool, Rumelt, Lencioni)

| Helps you say no (Spool) | yes: rejects entities knowable only by reading internals or asking maintainers | yes: rejects unstated cross-context reliance and out-of-band coordination | yes: rejects per-actor-kind rulebooks and recordless automation | yes: rejects designs that make below-level reading a prerequisite | yes: rejects silent drift and paper-only retirement | yes: rejects untraceable work and backlogs outside the product's contracts |
| Not fluff, not a goal-in-disguise (Rumelt) | pass — directs without prescribing method | pass | pass | pass | pass | pass |
| Not permission-to-play (Lencioni) | pass — most products are known by their code, not their descriptions | pass — most systems tolerate out-of-band coupling | pass — most shops rule humans and automations differently | pass — most systems require reading internals to work safely | pass — reverse conformance is rarely checked anywhere | pass — most backlogs live outside the product's audit trail |
| Implies ≥1 practice and ≥1 check (this document's intro) | description-at-creation practice; description-completeness audit | contract-first integration; unstated-reliance review | same-records-per-step authoring; actor-kind rule-text review | designated artifacts per level; below-level-read defect filing | design-change-first practice; two-direction conformance check | record-at-entry practice; originator-chain audit |

15	# ADR: Intent reaching the lead shop is recorded as a request on arrival and routed from that record
16	
17	## 1. Context
18	
19	The lead shop takes intent — a desired outcome expressed by an
20	originator at the product's edge; the initiative's word for one
21	expression of it is an *ask* — from the product authority, in
22	conversation. On 2026-09-04 the only door was the
23	[discovery conversation](../basis/processes/discovery-conversation.md):
24	it opens on a `topic` string (its parameter; the work item's title is
25	that string), frames an initiative, and hands it to the initiative
26	check and the authority's bet —
27	"the only door is discovery, the only path the full flow"
28	([init-request-routing](../initiatives/init-request-routing.md),
29	For whom). Intent arriving any other way — a direction given in a
30	session, a wish surfacing while another process runs ("backlog
31	requests", in the authority's words) — had no record of its own. It
32	was filed as a work item in the work register (`bd`, the beads tracker,
33	whose database stands at `/workspace/.beads`, outside this branch's
34	tree; an item carries a title and a close reason, and the discovery
35	conversation's own work item, lead-1kp6m, carries no description), or it stayed in the transcript. The
36	[`request` typedef](../basis/artifacts/request.md) (v2) defined the
37	type as the root for documents the shop *emits* — "any process whose
38	output asks for action or decision", `reader` required — the decision
39	brief to the authority being its one specialization; nothing the shop
40	received was a request. The first durable home an originator's words
41	had was the initiative's Framing, written only once a discovery
42	conversation had opened for them
43	([sess-2026-09-04-b](../sessions/sess-2026-09-04-b.md)).
44	
45	Forces bearing: `intent-provenance` — whoever accepts intent records
46	it at the contract where it entered before working on it, and the
47	lead shop's operational contract has no artifact on this branch
48	(lead-4kymc); the register pileup the authority named — "we have no
49	process for handling the pileup" — items that are asks with no durable
50	home. Working principles bearing:
51	`single-source-of-truth` — the originator's expression has one
52	authoritative home and every other appearance is a reference — and
53	`governed-context` — an agent works from a governed record, not a
54	transcript: the authority's "transition from transcript -> conversation
55	that has been missing"
56	([working principle set](../basis/principles.md)).
57	
58	**The escalation that settled it.** The decision is the authority's,
59	so it records under `right: escalation`: none of the five rights the
60	solutions architect role holds — stack, guardrail, decomposition,
61	contract between Bounded Contexts, non-functional requirement — covers
62	where intent enters the lead shop and as what record. The fork reached
63	the authority as the lead-pm's options in the discovery conversation
64	for init-request-routing on 2026-09-04 (lead-1kp6m, brainstorm form,
65	recorded in sess-2026-09-04-b), and the authority ruled in its words:
66	"I want request to become the front-end record for anything done by
67	the system, since we don't have a good entry-point to go from
68	open-ended human input to something an agent can work with", and
69	"Lead-pm should handle routing and all requests should be recorded and
70	rejection handled with the product authority, since the lead-pm is an
71	extension of the human authority." The ruling entered the initiative's
72	Document History (v1) and stands under the bet (v3). This record is
73	authored after the bet and before any definition amends, on the
74	authority's direction of the same day that the architect produce the
75	record the initiative rests on. The ruling bundled four positions;
76	this record carries the first, and the candidates list below names
77	the other three.
78	
79	Options that were real:
80	
81	- **Keep the work register as the record of an ask** — the standing
82	  practice for anything not yet framed. Declined for the authority's
83	  reason: "beads is not intended to be a system of record beyond
84	  current work in motion. Losing beads should not result in losing
85	  context about the system other than what is currently being
86	  executed." A register item is no artifact of a defined type — no
87	  typedef, no fitness set, no Document History, nothing in this
88	  branch's tree — so under `governed-context` an agent may not work
89	  from it as a governed record.
90	- **Open a discovery conversation for every ask** — the existing door.
91	  Declined: discovery frames an initiative for a bet, and a trivial
92	  functional change "shouldn't require a lot of process"; and the ask
93	  has no record until the conversation opens, the Framing quoting the
94	  originator only then.
95	- **A new artifact type for the received ask.** The authority weighed
96	  one — "a request specialization might be a separate artifact with a
97	  different name like 'small-feature-task'". Declined by the
98	  authority's direction, "we are not working through any new types",
99	  and because the `request` root already fits: a received ask is a
100	  document asking a reader to act or decide, the root's own
101	  definition, once the type admits one the shop receives.
102	- **Routing by a role other than the lead-pm** — a dedicated router
103	  role, one of the open amendments the branch primer lists. Not chosen: the authority placed routing with the
104	  lead-pm "since the lead-pm is an extension of the human authority"
105	  and made a decline an act taken with the authority; a router role,
106	  if it comes, would take the activity under this decision, not
107	  reopen it (see §4).
108	
109	Candidates split out under the one-decision rule, each the authority's
110	position from the same ruling (initiative history v1), taken here as
111	pre-state and decided by none of this record:
112	
113	- *The work register holds work in motion only* — the register's
114	  role.
115	- *The small-change lane is a feature with a size, framed by its
116	  request, not a new artifact type* — the lane's form.
117	- *Discovery accepts a request as its input and the initiative
118	  references it* — the hinge.
119	
120	Screened against the
121	[architecture principle set](../basis/architecture-principles.md):
122	conforms on five; `intent-provenance` is the principle the decision
123	cannot fully satisfy today, its exception escalated and carried by
124	lead-4kymc.
125	
126	- `intent-provenance` — not fully satisfied today. The principle
127	  requires intent to enter through a contract — for the lead shop, its
128	  operational contract — and this decision records intent at a record
129	  where that contract has no artifact: the request is the
130	  record-at-entry practice, each route a recorded translation on it,
131	  and the originator chain begins at a request, but the contract it
132	  enters through is stated nowhere. The exception is escalated to the
133	  authority and carried by lead-4kymc, the lead shop's operational
134	  contract having no artifact; conformance is restored when that
135	  artifact names the request as its entry record.
136	- `knowable-shape` — the lead shop's description of what it accepts
137	  gains a stated entry record and three stated routes, readable from
138	  the request typedef and the intake process's definition; nothing
139	  about what the shop takes in has to be learned from its internals.
140	- `contracts-between-contexts` — no Bounded Context is touched
141	  (the initiative's Decomposition); a request whose route reaches a
142	  shop travels only as scenario assignment sends it.
143	- `actor-neutral-discipline` — recording and routing attach to the
144	  lead-pm role in the intake process, with the same record whoever
145	  fills the role — the authority in person, agent-assisted, or an
146	  agent; "an extension of the human authority" states the role's
147	  standing, not a grant to an actor kind. A decline is the role's act
148	  with the authority, recorded on the request.
149	- `local-comprehension` — the request is a product-level record at the
150	  coordinating level; routing is performed from it alone, and a route
151	  into discovery hands on the record, never the transcript.
152	- `bidirectional-conformance` — the design change is recorded here
153	  before the definitions amend and the intake process runs; forward,
154	  the initiative's measure demonstrates it; reverse, the intake
155	  process's definition is what calls for each record the routing
156	  produces.
157	
158	One principle is not fully satisfied, its exception escalated as
159	named; no other principle is unsatisfied.
160	
161	## 2. Decision
162	
163	Every expression of intent the lead shop receives is recorded on
164	arrival as a `request` — the durable record, in the repository — and
165	routed from that record to one of three destinations: a discovery
166	conversation, the small-change lane — a path that takes a simple
167	change to a verified result without a bet or a screen of record — or a
168	decline settled with the product authority.
169	
170	## 3. Consequences
171	
172	- A record exists before any work. What changes: the request typedef
173	  must admit a received ask — the originator's words, the date, the
174	  route with its reason — and an intake process must carry the
175	  recording and the routing; the initiative's Feasibility names the
176	  amendments, their shape being the typedef owner's and the process
177	  author's. For whom: the lead-pm, which records and routes; anyone
178	  bringing the lead shop intent. Cost: a record per ask, declined
179	  asks included; the typedef amendment; one intake process with its
180	  screen rounds. Forecloses: acting on an unrecorded ask — a direction
181	  in a transcript or a register item is not a route.
182	- The routing activity is the lead-pm's. What changes: the intake
183	  process places recording and routing with the lead-pm role, on the
184	  authority's ruling that the lead-pm is "an extension of the human
185	  authority". For whom: the lead-pm; a router role, if one comes,
186	  takes the activity without reopening this decision. Cost: the
187	  lead-pm's session time per ask, the routing said before it is acted
188	  on.

# ADR: Intent reaching the lead shop is recorded as a request on arrival and routed from that record

## 1. Context

The lead shop takes intent — a desired outcome expressed by an
originator at the product's edge; the initiative's word for one
expression of it is an *ask* — from the product authority, in
conversation. On 2026-09-04 the only door was the
[discovery conversation](../basis/processes/discovery-conversation.md):
it opens on a `topic` string (its parameter; the work item's title is
that string), frames an initiative, and hands it to the initiative
check and the authority's bet —
"the only door is discovery, the only path the full flow"
([init-request-routing](../initiatives/init-request-routing.md),
For whom). Intent arriving any other way — a direction given in a
session, a wish surfacing while another process runs ("backlog
requests", in the authority's words) — had no record of its own. It
was filed as a work item in the work register (`bd`, the beads tracker,
whose database stands at `/workspace/.beads`, outside this branch's
tree; an item carries a title and a close reason, and the discovery
conversation's own work item, lead-1kp6m, carries no description), or it stayed in the transcript. The
[`request` typedef](../basis/artifacts/request.md) (v2) defined the
type as the root for documents the shop *emits* — "any process whose
output asks for action or decision", `reader` required — the decision
brief to the authority being its one specialization; nothing the shop
received was a request. The first durable home an originator's words
had was the initiative's Framing, written only once a discovery
conversation had opened for them
([sess-2026-09-04-b](../sessions/sess-2026-09-04-b.md)).

Forces bearing: `intent-provenance` — whoever accepts intent records
it at the contract where it entered before working on it, and the
lead shop's operational contract has no artifact on this branch
(lead-4kymc); the register pileup the authority named — "we have no
process for handling the pileup" — items that are asks with no durable
home. Working principles bearing:
`single-source-of-truth` — the originator's expression has one
authoritative home and every other appearance is a reference — and
`governed-context` — an agent works from a governed record, not a
transcript: the authority's "transition from transcript -> conversation
that has been missing"
([working principle set](../basis/principles.md)).

**The escalation that settled it.** The decision is the authority's,
so it records under `right: escalation`: none of the five rights the
solutions architect role holds — stack, guardrail, decomposition,
contract between Bounded Contexts, non-functional requirement — covers
where intent enters the lead shop and as what record. The fork reached
the authority as the lead-pm's options in the discovery conversation
for init-request-routing on 2026-09-04 (lead-1kp6m, brainstorm form,
recorded in sess-2026-09-04-b), and the authority ruled in its words:
"I want request to become the front-end record for anything done by
the system, since we don't have a good entry-point to go from
open-ended human input to something an agent can work with", and
"Lead-pm should handle routing and all requests should be recorded and
rejection handled with the product authority, since the lead-pm is an
extension of the human authority." The ruling entered the initiative's
Document History (v1) and stands under the bet (v3). This record is
authored after the bet and before any definition amends, on the
authority's direction of the same day that the architect produce the
record the initiative rests on. The ruling bundled four positions;
this record carries the first, and the candidates list below names
the other three.

Options that were real:

- **Keep the work register as the record of an ask** — the standing
  practice for anything not yet framed. Declined for the authority's
  reason: "beads is not intended to be a system of record beyond
  current work in motion. Losing beads should not result in losing
  context about the system other than what is currently being
  executed." A register item is no artifact of a defined type — no
  typedef, no fitness set, no Document History, nothing in this
  branch's tree — so under `governed-context` an agent may not work
  from it as a governed record.
- **Open a discovery conversation for every ask** — the existing door.
  Declined: discovery frames an initiative for a bet, and a trivial
  functional change "shouldn't require a lot of process"; and the ask
  has no record until the conversation opens, the Framing quoting the
  originator only then.
- **A new artifact type for the received ask.** The authority weighed
  one — "a request specialization might be a separate artifact with a
  different name like 'small-feature-task'". Declined by the
  authority's direction, "we are not working through any new types",
  and because the `request` root already fits: a received ask is a
  document asking a reader to act or decide, the root's own
  definition, once the type admits one the shop receives.
- **Routing by a role other than the lead-pm** — a dedicated router
  role, one of the open amendments the branch primer lists. Not chosen: the authority placed routing with the
  lead-pm "since the lead-pm is an extension of the human authority"
  and made a decline an act taken with the authority; a router role,
  if it comes, would take the activity under this decision, not
  reopen it (see §4).

Candidates split out under the one-decision rule, each the authority's
position from the same ruling (initiative history v1), taken here as
pre-state and decided by none of this record:

- *The work register holds work in motion only* — the register's
  role.
- *The small-change lane is a feature with a size, framed by its
  request, not a new artifact type* — the lane's form.
- *Discovery accepts a request as its input and the initiative
  references it* — the hinge.

Screened against the
[architecture principle set](../basis/architecture-principles.md):
conforms on five; `intent-provenance` is the principle the decision
cannot fully satisfy today, its exception escalated and carried by
lead-4kymc.

- `intent-provenance` — not fully satisfied today. The principle
  requires intent to enter through a contract — for the lead shop, its
  operational contract — and this decision records intent at a record
  where that contract has no artifact: the request is the
  record-at-entry practice, each route a recorded translation on it,
  and the originator chain begins at a request, but the contract it
  enters through is stated nowhere. The exception is escalated to the
  authority and carried by lead-4kymc, the lead shop's operational
  contract having no artifact; conformance is restored when that
  artifact names the request as its entry record.
- `knowable-shape` — the lead shop's description of what it accepts
  gains a stated entry record and three stated routes, readable from
  the request typedef and the intake process's definition; nothing
  about what the shop takes in has to be learned from its internals.
- `contracts-between-contexts` — no Bounded Context is touched
  (the initiative's Decomposition); a request whose route reaches a
  shop travels only as scenario assignment sends it.
- `actor-neutral-discipline` — recording and routing attach to the
  lead-pm role in the intake process, with the same record whoever
  fills the role — the authority in person, agent-assisted, or an
  agent; "an extension of the human authority" states the role's
  standing, not a grant to an actor kind. A decline is the role's act
  with the authority, recorded on the request.
- `local-comprehension` — the request is a product-level record at the
  coordinating level; routing is performed from it alone, and a route
  into discovery hands on the record, never the transcript.
- `bidirectional-conformance` — the design change is recorded here
  before the definitions amend and the intake process runs; forward,
  the initiative's measure demonstrates it; reverse, the intake
  process's definition is what calls for each record the routing
  produces.

One principle is not fully satisfied, its exception escalated as
named; no other principle is unsatisfied.

## 2. Decision

Every expression of intent the lead shop receives is recorded on
arrival as a `request` — the durable record, in the repository — and
routed from that record to one of three destinations: a discovery
conversation, the small-change lane — a path that takes a simple
change to a verified result without a bet or a screen of record — or a
decline settled with the product authority.

## 3. Consequences

- A record exists before any work. What changes: the request typedef
  must admit a received ask — the originator's words, the date, the
  route with its reason — and an intake process must carry the
  recording and the routing; the initiative's Feasibility names the
  amendments, their shape being the typedef owner's and the process
  author's. For whom: the lead-pm, which records and routes; anyone
  bringing the lead shop intent. Cost: a record per ask, declined
  asks included; the typedef amendment; one intake process with its
  screen rounds. Forecloses: acting on an unrecorded ask — a direction
  in a transcript or a register item is not a route.
- The routing activity is the lead-pm's. What changes: the intake
  process places recording and routing with the lead-pm role, on the
  authority's ruling that the lead-pm is "an extension of the human
  authority". For whom: the lead-pm; a router role, if one comes,
  takes the activity without reopening this decision. Cost: the
  lead-pm's session time per ask, the routing said before it is acted
  on.
- A decline is not the lead-pm's alone. What changes: the third
  destination is a decision taken with the authority and recorded on
  the request. For whom: the lead-pm; the authority, whose ruling each
  decline needs. Cost: the authority's attention per decline; a
  silent drop is no longer possible.
- The register is not the record of an ask. What changes: a work item
  opened for a routed ask points at its request, and what was asked is
  read from the request, never from the item. For whom: whoever opens
  or reads items. Cost: the reference on every such item. The wider
  rule — the register holds work in motion only — is the first
  candidate in §1, not decided here.
- Intent met mid-process has somewhere to go. What changes: a role
  that meets an ask while running another process records it as a
  request and continues, instead of acting on it or losing it. For
  whom: every lead-shop role. Cost: a record written outside the
  running step; its route waits for the lead-pm.
- Provenance starts at the request. What changes: a trace that
  dead-ends before a request is a recording defect; the initiative's
  Framing and the small-change path's work must reach the request. For
  whom: reviewers demanding the originator chain; the PM role at
  framing. Cost: the reference from each; whether the Framing quotes
  or references the originator's words is the third candidate in §1.

Bound on Bounded Context shops: none — a BC shop's intake stands under
its own operational contract; extending this decision to it would be a
guardrail decision, the architect role's.

## 4. Reversibility

Reversible at low cost until requests carry provenance: reverting is
amending the request typedef back to an emitted-only type and retiring
the intake process — design first, the reverse conformance check then
naming the process and its renderings for retirement. Hard once
initiatives and features name a request as their origin: each such
reference becomes a dead-ended trace under `intent-provenance` unless
the originator's words move back into the referencing document, one
edit per record. Review triggers: the lead shop's operational contract
artifact (lead-4kymc) landing with a different entry record; a router
role taking the routing activity from the lead-pm; a volume of
requests the lead-pm cannot route within a session; a Bounded
Context's product contract accepting intent directly, so that the lead
shop's front end is no longer the only one.
